香港警方拘捕小巴司机涉嫌毒驾七名乘客安全疏散中国劳工公告栏
2026 年 11 月 10 日，星期二 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻（英文）
香港警方拘捕小巴司机涉嫌毒驾 七名乘客安全疏散
香港警方拘捕一名44岁小巴司机，涉嫌吸食冰毒后驾驶。七名乘客被安全疏散。司机被拒绝保释，将于 11 月 11 日出庭。警方警告公共交通司机不要毒驾。
香港警方在打击公务车辆司机毒驾的专项行动中，拘捕了一名涉嫌吸毒后驾驶的44岁男性小巴司机。
东九龙总区交通分区行政及管制组高级督察潘俊豪表示，今年六月，警方拘捕了三名涉嫌毒驾的小巴和的士司机。这导致了 11 月 10 日的有针对性的部署，当时警方发现一名小巴司机在油塘和安德森之间的路线上行驶。警方安全拦截了小巴，并从车上疏散了七名乘客。快速口腔液测试表明司机在开车前服用了甲基苯丙胺。他立即被捕。
该司机被拒绝保释，案件将于11月11日在观塘裁判法院审理。
警方表示，他们非常严肃地对待公务车辆司机毒驾的行为。在六月的行动中，三名司机被捕，其中两人被定罪，分别被判处两个月和四个月监禁，并分别被取消驾驶资格两年和五年。第三名司机已保释候审。
警方强调，此类行为并非简单的违法行为，而是对乘客和其他道路使用者的生命构成严重威胁。他们表示，一名司机故意服用影响判断力和反应的药物，却驾驶公共交通车辆，这将使所有乘客处于极度危险之中，一旦发生事故，后果将是灾难性的。警方将继续以情报为主导的执法行动，打击此类严重的交通违法行为。

Hong Kong police arrest minibus driver for suspected drug-driving, seven passengers safely evacuated | China Labour Bulletin Board
Tuesday, 10 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong police arrest minibus driver for suspected drug-driving, seven passengers safely evacuated
Hong Kong police arrested a 44-year-old minibus driver on suspicion of driving after taking methamphetamine. Seven passengers were safely evacuated. The driver was denied bail and will appear in court on 11 November. Police warn against drug-driving by public transport drivers.
Hong Kong police have arrested a 44-year-old male minibus driver on suspicion of driving after taking drugs, in a targeted operation against drug-driving by public service vehicle drivers.
Senior Inspector Poon Chun-ho of the Kowloon East Regional Traffic Division Executive and Control Group said that in June this year, police arrested three minibus and taxi drivers on suspicion of drug-driving. That led to a targeted deployment on 10 November, when officers identified a minibus driver operating a route between Yau Tong and Anderson. Police safely stopped the minibus and evacuated seven passengers from the vehicle. A rapid oral fluid test indicated the driver had taken methamphetamine before driving. He was arrested immediately.
The driver has been denied bail and his case will be heard at Kwun Tong Magistrates' Court on 11 November.
Police said they treat drug-driving by public service vehicle drivers very seriously. In the June operation, three drivers were arrested, of whom two have been convicted and sentenced to two months' and four months' imprisonment, with driving disqualifications of two years and five years respectively. The third driver is on bail awaiting trial.
Police emphasised that such behaviour is not a simple violation but poses a serious threat to the lives of passengers and other road users. They said a driver who knowingly takes drugs that impair judgment and reaction, yet drives a public transport vehicle, is putting all passengers in extreme danger, and the consequences of an accident would be catastrophic. Police will continue intelligence-led enforcement against such serious traffic offences.

title: Independent Hong Kong book fair urges transparency after 5 exhibitors barred under ‘force majeure’
zh_title: 5家参展商因“不可抗力”被禁止，香港独立书展敦促透明度

content:
据称，五家参展商被当局禁止参展，且没有给出任何解释，香港独立书展的组织者呼吁公开和透明。香港独立书展Duk6 Duk6的海报。照片：Duk6 Duk6。 Duk6 Duk6是一个推广自行出版作品的“独立叙事图书节”，第四届将于11月14日至15日在荃湾南丰纱厂举行。据本地创作者非营利团体 Yun Hyun 介绍，今年的展会将有约 125 家参展商展示漫画、小说、杂志、动画和游戏。但组织者周末表示，由于“不可抗力”，五家参展商被取消了参展资格。 “我们最近收到有关部门的通知，称由于许可过程中出现不可抗力问题，某些参展商无法参加，”尹炫在社交媒体上用中文发帖表示，但没有具体说明涉及的政府部门。不可抗力——涵盖双方无法控制的事件的合同条款——是场地和活动合同的主要内容。然而，近年来，对于许多香港人来说，这个词越来越成为隐秘政治压力和审查制度的代名词。尹贤没有透露哪些参展商必须退出，只表示受影响的参展商包括漫画、小说作家和插画家。
该组织补充说，他们的作品主题广泛，从香港本土文化到科幻小说。该组织还呼吁当局明确审查制度，以便活动组织者能够更好地合作。 “近年来，类似的活动经常遇到类似的情况。希望相关部门能够有一个更加公开透明的机制，让创作者和组织者更容易合作。”尹贤说。 “我们不知道界线在哪里” 一位因担心遭到报复而不愿透露姓名的艺博会策展人告诉《香港新闻社》，组织者一直在向食物环境卫生署（食环署）寻求临时公众娱乐场所许可证。馆长表示，申请必须经过多个部门的审核。 “有一个部门打电话告诉我们，要么这五家参展商必须被移除，要么整个活动将被取消，但没有给出任何解释，”策展人说。 HKFP已联系食环署征求意见。策展人补充说，上一届书展于 2025 年初举办，也遭遇了场馆管理部门针对特定参展商的审查。 2025 年 Duk6 Duk6 书展。照片：Duk6 Duk6。 “鉴于这次经历，并看到最近每一个类似的活动都面临着同样的障碍，我们当然做好了准备，”策展人说。
“不过，我们没想到一下子就有五个参展商被 DQ [取消资格]。”策展人表示，所有 125 家参展商都是经过精心挑选的，以确保不出现人工智能生成或抄袭的材料，并补充说，该活动的布局是为了将志同道合的艺术家聚集在一起而起草的。策展人表示，现阶段失去 5 家参展商大大增加了团队审查替代品的工作量，并有可能破坏精心策划的布局。策展人说，突然的排除也给供应商带来了沉重打击，他们花了几个月的时间准备在活动中推出新作品。 “其实每个人都想继续，但我们不知道界限在哪里，”

【原文 English Original】
Organisers of an independent Hong Kong book fair have called for openness and transparency after five exhibitors were allegedly barred by authorities without explanation. The poster of Duk6 Duk6, an independent book fair in Hong Kong. Photo: Duk6 Duk6. Duk6 Duk6, an “indie narrative book fest” that promotes self-published works, is set to hold its fourth edition on November 14 and 15 at The Mills in Tsuen Wan. This year’s fair will feature about 125 exhibitors showcasing comics, novels, zines, animation and games, according to Yun Hyun, a non-profit collective of local creators. But organisers said over the weekend that five exhibitors had been disqualified from the event due to “force majeure.” “We recently received notifications from relevant authorities stating that, owing to force majeure issues arising during the licensing process, certain exhibitors cannot participate,” Yun Hyun said in a social media post written in Chinese, without specifying the government departments involved. Force majeure – a contract clause covering events beyond the parties’ control – is a staple of venue and event contracts. Yet for many in Hong Kong in recent years, the phrase has increasingly become shorthand for covert political pressure and censorship . Yun Hyun did not name the exhibitors that had to withdraw, only saying that the affected exhibitors included comic and novel writers and illustrators. The themes of their works range from local Hong Kong culture to science fiction, the group added. The group also called on the authorities to provide clarity regarding censorship, so that event organisers can better cooperate. “In recent years, similar events have frequently encountered similar situations. It is hoped that relevant departments will have a more open and transparent mechanism to make it easier for creators and organisers to cooperate,” Yun Hyun said. ‘We don’t know where the line is’ A curator of the fair, speaking on condition of anonymity citing fear of reprisals, told HKFP that organisers had been seeking a Temporary Places of Public Entertainment Licence from the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD). The application had to go through multiple departments for vetting, the curator said. “One department called and told us that either these five exhibitors had to be removed, or the whole event would be cancelled, without giving any explanation,” the curator said. HKFP has reached out to the FEHD for comment. The curator added that the last edition of the book fair, held in early 2025, also encountered censorship against specific exhibitors by venue management. The Duk6 Duk6 book fair in 2025. Photo: Duk6 Duk6. “Given that experience, and seeing how every similar event lately has faced the same roadblocks, we were of course braced for it,” the curator said. “Still, we never imagined five exhibitors would be DQ’d [disqualified] in one go.” The curator said all 125 exhibitors were hand-picked to ensure no AI-generated or plagiarised material was featured, adding that the event’s layout was drafted to bring like-minded artists together. Losing five exhibitors at this stage added significantly to the team’s workload in vetting replacements and threatened to disrupt the carefully planned layout, the curator said. The sudden exclusions also dealt a heavy blow to the vendors, who had spent months preparing to debut new work at the event, the curator said. “Actually everyone wants to continue, but we don’t know where the line is drawn,” the curator said. “And we are not even trying to cross any lines, but even harmless things could be DQ’d.” “The economic environment in recent years has been poor, and coupled with the impact of AI, the entire creative community is facing great challenges,” the curator added. “As organisers, we hope that every creator and their work can be seen. But there’s only so much we can do.”

content:
资助机会通知 (NOFO)：在斯威士兰举办 2027 GCTF 研讨会 资助机会通知 (NOFO) 在斯威士兰美国台湾学院举办 2027 G CTF 研讨会 机会编号：GCTF-TAIPEI-FY2 7 -00 1 申请截止日期：202 年 11 月 23 日 6 日晚上 11:59 （台北时间） A. 基本信息 1. 概述 资助方式：合作协议。合作协议包括局或大使馆实质性参与项目的计划实施。下文 C.2 节包含实质性参与的示例。项目实施期限：拟建项目应于202年5月31日前完成 7．本通知视资金情况而定。公共外交部门保留在被认为符合美国政府最佳利益的情况下授予少于或超过所述资金的权利，具体取决于资金的可用性和指定拨款官员的批准。 2. 执行摘要 美国在台协会 (AIT) 公共外交部门 (PDS) 宣布开展一项合作协议公开竞赛，以支持 2027 年第一季度或第二季度在斯威士兰规划和实施全球合作与培训框架 (GCTF) 区域特许经营研讨会。在资金允许的情况下，AIT 打算授予一份约 20 万美元的合作协议来实施该计划。
全球合作与培训框架（GCTF）是一个国际能力建设平台，汇集了政府官员、技术专家、行业代表、学者和民间社会代表，交流实践经验并加强应对区域和全球挑战的合作。GCTF由台湾和美国于2015年成立，此后扩大到包括日本、澳大利亚、加拿大和英国作为合作伙伴。拟议的研讨会“加强南部非洲的网络安全和数字治理”预计将于 2027 年第一季度或第二季度在斯威士兰举行。该计划将重点关注加强网络安全弹性、改善数字治理、保护关键数字基础设施、应对新出现的网络威胁以及促进安全和可信的数字转型。它将为参与者提供一个交流实践经验、确定共同挑战、加强专业网络和区域合作的平台。该研讨会预计将包括来自至少八个非洲国家的代表，特别强调南部非洲的区域参与。第一天预计将有约 60 至 80 名参与者参加，活动内容包括全体讨论、专家演讲和实践交流。
预计第二天将有约 40 名参与者参加，其中可能包括重点技术讨论、互动练习、工作组会议和/或相关现场参观。该计划预计将汇集来自参与非洲国家的政府官员、网络安全和数字治理从业者、技术专家、私营部门代表、学者、民间社会代表和其他相关利益攸关方。来自美国、台湾和其他 GCTF 合作伙伴（包括日本、澳大利亚、加拿大）的主题专家

【原文 English Original】
Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO): Implementation of 2027 GCTF Workshop in Eswatini Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) Implementation of 2027 G CTF Workshop in Eswatini American Institute in Taiwan Opportunity number: GCTF-TAIPEI-FY2 7 -00 1 Application deadline: November 23 , 202 6 , at 11:59 p.m. (Taipei Time)   A. Basic Information 1. Overview Funding Instrument Type: C ooperative agreement . Cooperative agreements include substantial involvement of the bureau or embassy in program implementation of the project. Examples of substantial involvement are included in section C.2 below. Project Performance Period : Proposed projects should be completed by May 31 , 202 7 . This notice is subject to availability of funding. The Public Diplomacy Section reserves the right to award less or more than the funds described under circumstances deemed to be in the best interest of the U.S. government, pending the availability of funds and approval of the designated grants officer. 2. Executive Summary The American Institute in Taiwan (AIT) Public Diplomacy Section (PDS) announces an open competition for a cooperative agreement to support the planning and implementation of a Global Cooperation and Training Framework (GCTF) regional franchise workshop in Eswatini in the first or second quarter of 2027. Subject to the availability of funding, AIT intends to award one cooperative agreement of approximately USD 200,000 to implement this program. The Global Cooperation and Training Framework (GCTF) is an international capacity-building platform that brings together government officials, technical experts, industry representatives, academics, and civil society representatives to exchange practical experiences and strengthen cooperation in addressing regional and global challenges. The GCTF was established by Taiwan and the United States in 2015 and has since expanded to include Japan, Australia, Canada, and the United Kingdom as Partners. The proposed workshop, “Strengthening Cybersecurity and Digital Governance in Southern Africa,” is expected to take place in Eswatini during the first or second quarter of 2027. The program will focus on strengthening cybersecurity resilience, improving digital governance, protecting critical digital infrastructure, addressing emerging cyber threats, and promoting secure and trusted digital transformation. It will provide a platform for participants to exchange practical experiences, identify common challenges, and strengthen professional networks and regional cooperation. The workshop is expected to include representatives from at least eight African countries, with a particular emphasis on regional participation from Southern Africa. Approximately 60 to 80 participants are expected to participate in the first day of the program, which will feature plenary discussions, expert presentations, and practical exchanges. A smaller group of approximately 40 participants is expected to participate in the second day, which may include focused technical discussions, interactive exercises, working-group sessions, and/or relevant site visits. The program is expected to bring together government officials, cybersecurity and digital governance practitioners, technical experts, private-sector representatives, academics, civil society representatives, and other relevant stakeholders from participating African countries. Subject-matter experts from the United States, Taiwan, and other GCTF Partners, including Japan, Australia, Canada, and the United Kingdom, may also be invited to contribute relevant international expertise and practical experience. The selected recipient will serve as AIT’s implementation partner and will be responsible for comprehensive program and logistical support, including venue and lodging coordination, participant management, travel arrangements for designated participants and speakers, ground transportation, interpretation and audiovisual services, workshop materials, vendor coordination, monitoring and evaluation, and required grant reporting. Travel expenses for U.S. Government officials invited by the U.S. Government and Taiwan-supported speakers will be funded separately and should not be included in the recipient’s proposed budget. AIT and GCTF partners will provide overall policy guidance, strategic direction, and substantive oversight throughout program planning and implementation. Eligible applicants include nonprofit organizations, educational institutions, professional associations, think tanks, private-sector organizations with relevant international program management experience, public international organizations where eligible under applicable U.S. Government regulations, and other eligible organizations with demonstrated capacity to organize international conferences or capacity-building programs and administer U.S. Government assistance awards. This cooperative agreement is intended to strengthen practical cybersecurity capacity and digital governance cooperation in Southern Africa, expand professional and institutional connections among participating countries, and advance the GCTF as a platform for practical international capacity building, technical exchange, and sustained regional cooperation. B. Eligibility 1. Eligible Applicants The following organizations are eligible to apply: Not-for-profit organizations , including non-governmental organizations (NGOs), think tanks, and civil society organizations Educational institutions , including universities and research institutions Professional associations and nonprofit organizations with demonstrated experience managing international conferences or capacity-building programs Private-sector organizations with demonstrated experience organizing international conferences or implementing international exchange programs Public international organizations , where eligible under applicable U.S. Government regulations Organizations may sub-contract with other entities, but only one entity, from the eligible categories of organizations listed above, can be the prime recipient of the award. When sub-contracting with other entities, the responsibilities of each entity must be clearly defined in the proposal. For more information on the difference between sub-contract and sub-recipient, please refer to 2 CFR 200 .331 . 2. Cost Sharing or Matching Cost sharing is not required . 3. Other Eligibility Requirements All organizations must have a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) issued via SAM.gov as well as a valid registration in SAM.gov. Please see Section D.3 for more information. Individuals are not required to have a UEI or be registered in SAM.gov. Applicants are only allowed to submit one proposal per organization. If more than one proposal is submitted from an organization, all proposals from that institution will be considered ineligible for funding. 4. This opportunity will not support: Projects relating to partisan political activity; Charitable or development activities; including direct social services such as medical, psychological, and/or humanitarian support Construction projects; Projects that support specific religious activities; Fund-raising campaigns; Lobbying for specific legislation or programs Scientific research or surveys; Commercial projects; Projects intended primarily for the growth or institutional development of the organization; Projects that duplicate existing projects; Illegal activities C. Program Description 1. Project Background, Goals, and Objectives Project Background The Global Cooperation and Training Framework (GCTF) is an international capacity-building platform established by Taiwan and the United States in 2015. Japan joined as a full partner in 2019, followed by Australia in 2021, Canada in 2023, and the United Kingdom in 2025. Through workshops and other capacity-building activities, GCTF brings together government officials, technical experts, industry representatives, and civil society representatives to exchange practical experience, strengthen professional networks, and develop approaches to shared regional and global challenges. As governments and societies become increasingly dependent on digital technologies and interconnected systems, cybersecurity and effective digital governance have become important elements of economic development, public-service delivery, critical infrastructure resilience, and public trust. Recent research documents that scam syndicates displaced from Southeast Asian epicenters, including Myanmar, Laos, and Cambodia, are actively pivoting to Africa, with documented raids in nine African countries and growing evidence of scam infrastructure, including online gambling platforms used as cover for fraud operations, gray business Telegram groups openly advertising scam facilities, and unregulated cryptocurrency services establishing footholds across the continent. Countries across Southern Africa face evolving cybersecurity and cybercrime challenges while also seeking to expand digital services, strengthen institutional capacity, and develop governance frameworks that support secure and trusted digital transformation. The proposed GCTF regional workshop in Eswatini will provide a platform for government officials, cybersecurity and the digital governance practitioners, technical experts, private-sector representatives, academics, civil society representatives, and other relevant stakeholders from across Africa to exchange practical experiences and strengthen professional and institutional connections. The workshop is expected to include representatives from at least eight African countries, with particular emphasis on participation from Southern Africa. The program will draw on expertise and practical experience from participating African countries as well as the United States, Taiwan, and other GCTF partners, as appropriate. Through expert presentations, policy and technical discussions, interactive exchanges, and other practical activities, the workshop will address shared challenges and identify approaches that participating countries may adapt to their respective national and institutional contexts. Strengthening cybersecurity capacity and secure digital governance in Southern Africa also advances U.S. security and economic interests. Cyber threats, cyber-enabled crime, and vulnerabilities in interconnected digital systems increasingly cross-national borders and can affect American citizens, businesses, and critical infrastructure. By strengthening the ability of partner countries to prevent, identify, respond to, and recover from cyber threats, this program can help reduce vulnerabilities that may be exploited by transnational criminal networks and other malicious cyber actors. The workshop will also strengthen U.S. engagement with African partners on secure and resilient digital ecosystems, promote cooperation and information sharing among governments and technical experts, and expand relationships between African stakeholders and the United States and other GCTF partners. Through practical capacity building and sustained professional networks, the program will support a more secure and resilient regional digital environment while advancing shared interests in cybersecurity, economic security, and trusted digital development. Project Goal: The goal of this project is to strengthen cybersecurity resilience and digital governance capacity in Southern Africa by facilitating practical knowledge exchange, regional cooperation, and sustained professional engagement among participating countries and international partners, while advancing shared U.S. and partner interests in a more secure, resilient, and trusted digital environment. Project Objectives: The project will pursue the following objectives: Strengthen Cybersecurity Capacity and Resilience: Enhance participants’ knowledge of practical approaches to preventing, preparing for, responding to, and recovering from cybersecurity threats and incidents, with a specific focus on basic cyber hygiene, national cyber resilience, digital trust, and the development of a secure digital ecosystem aligned with global standards and best practices. Advance Effective and Secure Digital Governance: Promote the exchange of policies, practices, institutional approaches, and lessons learned that support secure, trusted, resilient, and inclusive digital governance and digital transformation. Promote Regional Cooperation and Information Sharing: Strengthen professional and institutional connections among participating African countries and encourage greater cross-border cooperation, information sharing, and coordination in addressing shared cybersecurity and digital governance challenges. Facilitate Practical International Exchange: Connect African policymakers and practitioners with relevant expertise and practical experience from participating African countries, the United States, Taiwan, and other GCTF partner countries, including Japan, Australia, Canada, and the United Kingdom, as appropriate to the workshop agenda. Support Sustainable Professional Networks and Follow-on Cooperation: Encourage participants to identify practical opportunities for continued professional engagement, knowledge sharing, and future cooperation beyond the workshop. 2. Substantial Involvement This award will require substantial involvement from the American Institute in Taiwan (AIT ) and the U . S . Embassy in Eswatini . AIT will approve all key aspects of the workshop, including but not limited to venue selection, flight and hotel arrangements, ground transportation, lodging, visual designs, agenda, site visit locations, speaker and participant lists, catering and menus, conference room layout, lighting, and audio-visual setup. In cases of more than one FADR Data Element, typically program or sector and/or regions or country, the successful applicant will be required to maintain separate accounting records. If the federal share of the award will include more than $500,000 over the period of performance, insert the following language: Applicants should be aware of the post award reporting requirements reflected in 2 CFR 200 Appendix XII—Award Term and Condition for Recipient Integrity and Performance Matters . 3.Branding and Marking The Department of State, its programs, and U.S. Government funding and assistance should be easily identifiable to the Department’s global audiences. title: Nvidia announces probe into CEO Jensen Huang after he acknowledges affair with alleged Chinese spy
zh_title: 英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋承认与涉嫌中国间谍有染后，宣布对他进行调查
summary: 芯片巨头英伟达董事会周日宣布，在首席执行官兼联合创始人黄仁勋承认与一名美国官员称为中国情报机构工作的女性有染后，对他展开调查。 Nvidia 创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋于 2026 年 1 月 5 日在内华达州拉斯维加斯举行的年度消费电子展之前，在 CES 2026 的 Nvidia Live 上发表讲话。照片：Patrick T. Fallon/法新社。上个月末，《纽约时报》报道称，美国情报官员得出的结论是，这名女子是一名与新加坡一家名为 Megaspeed 的数据中心公司有联系的中国高管。
content:
芯片巨头英伟达董事会周日宣布，在首席执行官兼联合创始人黄仁勋承认与一名美国官员称为中国情报机构工作的女性有染后，对他展开调查。 Nvidia 创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋于 2026 年 1 月 5 日在内华达州拉斯维加斯举行的年度消费电子展之前，在 CES 2026 的 Nvidia Live 上发表讲话。照片：Patrick T. Fallon/法新社。上个月末，《纽约时报》报道称，美国情报官员得出的结论是，这名女子是一名与新加坡一家名为 Megaspeed 的数据中心公司有联系的中国高管，一直在向北京输送信息。据《泰晤士报》报道，这位高管爱丽丝·黄（Alice Huang）——又名黄乐，与 63 岁的台湾出生的黄仁勋没有任何关系——与 Nvidia 老板建立了密切的关系。在周日发布的致公司员工的信息中，黄承认有外遇，并向家人和公司员工道歉。 “我对我的妻子不忠，”他说。 “我的行为伤害了她和我们的孩子。我的所作所为没有任何借口。我深感抱歉。”黄仁勋是人工智能革命的重要人物，也是唐纳德·特朗普总统的亲密非正式顾问，特朗普多次公开反对监管该行业，以免让中国在人工智能竞赛中占据上风。 《泰晤士报》称，黄与另一位黄的关系可能让她深入了解特朗普对人工智能的看法。
特朗普计划于本月晚些时候在中国举行的峰会上与习近平主席举行会谈，人工智能问题可能会出现。英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋在华盛顿特区安德鲁·W·梅隆礼堂举行的白宫人工智能峰会上。 2025 年 7 月 23 日。照片：白宫，来自 Flickr。英伟达在一份声明中表示，“鉴于最近有报道称创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋已成为外国情报机构的目标”，该公司已展开独立调查。声明补充道：“虽然委员会没有理由相信国家安全或 NVIDIA 机密受到损害，但委员会的调查将检查所有可用信息。”周日被问及黄的情况时，特朗普告诉记者：“我只知道他是一个好人，但你永远不知道发生了什么。我确信——我希望一切都好。他做了如此令人难以置信的工作。”中国政府驳斥了《纽约时报》的报道，称其为“毫无根据的猜测”。 “黑眼圈时刻” 中国正在与美国争夺科技主导地位，美国限制了最尖端硅芯片向中国的出口。英伟达是生产用于训练和运行人工智能模型的芯片的全球领导者，也是世界上最有价值的公司之一。 《泰晤士报》援引未透露姓名的知情人士的话报道称，Megaspeed 因可能将 Nvidia 人工智能芯片转移到中国而受到审查。
据《泰晤士报》报道，特朗普大约一年前获悉有关黄与这位女商人关系的情报调查结果，并选择不对这些信息采取行动。特朗普周日表示，他并不后悔没有对这一情报采取行动。 “不，我不这么认为。我认为——你知道，他是一个值得尊敬的人。我认为他可能有一个借口。你必须听到它。” Nvidia 创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋于 2025 年 5 月 19 日在台湾台北举行的 Computex 2025 上发表主题演讲。照片：Nvidia。投资银行约克维尔艾夫斯 (Yorkville Ives) 的技术分析师丹·艾夫斯 (Dan Ives) 表示，调查的消息对黄仁勋来说是“一个沉重的时刻”。艾夫斯预测这至少会引起人们的注意

【原文 English Original】
Chip giant Nvidia’s board announced Sunday it opened a probe into Chief Executive and co-founder Jensen Huang after he acknowledged an affair with a woman US officials say was working for Chinese intelligence. Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang speaks during Nvidia Live at CES 2026 ahead of the annual Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas, Nevada, on January 5, 2026. Photo: Patrick T. Fallon/AFP. Late last month, The New York Times reported that US intelligence officials concluded that the woman, a Chinese executive linked to a Singapore-based data center company called Megaspeed, had been funnelling information to Beijing. The executive, Alice Huang — also known as Huang Le, and no relation to 63-year-old Taiwanese-born Jensen Huang — developed a close relationship with the Nvidia boss, the Times said. In a message to company employees released Sunday, Huang acknowledged having an affair and apologized to his family and company staff. “I was unfaithful to my wife,” he said. “My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.” Jensen Huang is a huge figure in the artificial intelligence revolution and a close informal adviser to President Donald Trump, who has repeatedly spoken out against regulating the industry so as not to let China gain the upper hand in the AI race. The Times said Huang’s relationship with the other Huang could have given her insights into Trump’s thinking around AI. The issue of AI is likely to arise during Trump’s planned talks with President Xi Jinping later this month at a summit in China. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang at the White House AI Summit at Andrew W. Mellon Auditorium in Washington, DC. on July 23, 2025. Photo: The White House, via Flickr. Nvidia said in a statement it opened an independent probe “in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” The statement added: “While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised , the Board’s inquiry will examine all available information.” Asked about Huang on Sunday, Trump told reporters: “I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what’s going on. I’m sure — I hope everything’s fine. He’s done such an incredible job.” The Chinese government has dismissed the Times report as “groundless speculation.” ‘Black eye moment’ China is in a race for tech dominance with the United States, which restricts the export to China of the most cutting-edge silicon chips. Nvidia, a global leader in producing chips used to train and run AI models, is one of the world’s most valuable companies. Megaspeed was under scrutiny for possibly steering Nvidia AI chips to China, the Times report said, citing unnamed sources briefed on the matter. Trump was briefed on the intelligence findings about Huang’s relationship with the businesswoman roughly a year ago and chose not to act on the information, the Times report said. Trump said Sunday he did not regret not acting on this intelligence. “No, I don’t think so. I think — you know, he’s an honorable guy. I think he probably has an excuse for it. You have to hear it.” Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang gives a keynote speech at Computex 2025 in Taipei, Taiwan, on May 19, 2025. Photo: Nvidia. Technology analyst Dan Ives, with the investment bank Yorkville Ives, said word of the probe is “a black eye moment” for Jensen Huang. Ives predicted it will at the very least spark multiple congressional inquiries and “create an overhang on the stock for a myriad of reasons.” In the near-term Huang is expected to keep his job but risks being removed as Nvidia’s CEO depending on the board’s probe, Ives said in a statement. “This will add risk to the stock as he is so important to the Nvidia story and strategy globally,” he said. “This will also increase major scrutiny regarding selling chips to China, which remains a key battleground issue in DC.”

summary: 萨尔田港拓展APEC航线提升深圳物流枢纽地位中国劳工布告栏 星期二, 10 Nov 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工英文新闻 萨尔田港拓展 APEC 航线，提升深圳物流枢纽地位 萨尔田港今年新增 14 条 APEC 航线，凸显了深圳作为其经济支柱的现代物流业。港口利用AI、5G智慧运营，铁海联运系统连接香港葵青货柜码头，提升供应 亚太经合组织峰会
content:
萨尔田港拓展APEC航线提升深圳物流枢纽地位中国劳工公告栏
2026 年 11 月 10 日，星期二 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻（英文）
盐田港拓展APEC航线提升深圳物流枢纽地位
盐田港今年新增14条APEC航线，凸显了深圳现代物流业的经济支柱。港口利用AI、5G智慧运营，铁海联运系统连接香港葵青货柜码头，提升供应能力
亚太经合组织（APEC）峰会将在中国第一个经济特区深圳举行。 40多年前，深圳从一个小渔村发展成为国内生产总值排名全国第三位的经济强国。现代物流是全市四大支柱产业之一，约占全市经济总量的10%。市政府数据显示，去年深圳货运总量突破3.7亿吨，港口集装箱吞吐量突破3500万标准箱，增长超5%，创开港以来新高。深圳港目前是全球第四大集装箱枢纽港。
盐田港位于深圳东南部，1994年开始运营，现有20个大型深水泊位。它是全球最大的单体集装箱码头之一，每周运营近100条国际航线，其中53条连接APEC成员经济体。萨尔田国际集装箱码头董事总经理岑其成表示，该港不断扩大区域贸易联系，今年新增14条APEC航线。尽管国际形势动荡，他仍对确保供应链稳定表示信心。
岑表示，萨尔田港正在加快智慧码头建设，从传统劳动密集型物流向现代智慧物流转变。这包括使用人工智能分析多艘船舶的同时操作，以及使用 5G 网络更精确地控制起重机系统。操作人员不再需要长时间在室外驾驶室工作，而是可以从控制室远程控制大型装卸设备，大大提高了运输、装卸和配送的效率和可靠性。
铁海联运是现代物流不可或缺的要素。岑表示，盐田口岸是深圳唯一铁路列车可直达的口岸。从重庆、成都等内陆地区通过铁路运输至萨尔田港的货物，可通过驳船转运至香港葵青货柜码头出口至国际市场。这一模式大大缩短了运输时间，提高了中国西部地区的出口效率。
索尔天国际是长和集团旗下和记港口网络的成员。深圳“十五五”规划纲要强调加强盐田港与香港葵青港的合作。目前，每天有六艘驳船往返于萨尔田和香港之间，大约在六至八小时内完成双向货物运输。岑表示，两港互补性强，可以进一步开发内陆货源，共同实现“盐田—葵青”枢纽功能，支撑国家外贸高质量发展。

【原文 English Original】
Saltian Port Expands APEC Routes, Boosts Shenzhen Logistics Hub Status | China Labour Bulletin Board
Tuesday, 10 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Saltian Port Expands APEC Routes, Boosts Shenzhen Logistics Hub Status
Shenzhen's modern logistics industry, a pillar of its economy, is highlighted by Saltian Port's expansion of 14 new APEC shipping routes this year. The port uses AI and 5G for smart operations, and its rail-sea intermodal system links to Hong Kong's Kwai Tsing Container Terminals, enhancing supply c
The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit is set to be held in Shenzhen, China's first special economic zone. From a small fishing village over 40 years ago, Shenzhen has grown into an economic powerhouse ranking third in national GDP. Modern logistics is one of its four pillar industries, accounting for about 10 per cent of the city's total economic output. According to municipal government data, Shenzhen's total freight volume last year exceeded 370 million tonnes, and its port container throughput surpassed 35 million standard units, a growth of over 5 per cent and a record high since the port opened. Shenzhen Port is currently the world's fourth-largest container hub port.
Located in southeastern Shenzhen, Saltian Port began operations in 1994 and now has 20 large deep-water berths. It is one of the world's largest single container terminals, operating nearly 100 international shipping routes per week, 53 of which connect to APEC member economies. Saltian International Container Terminal Managing Director Cen Qicheng said the port continues to expand regional trade links, adding 14 new APEC routes this year. Despite a volatile international situation, he expressed confidence in ensuring supply chain stability.
Moving from traditional labour-intensive logistics to modern smart logistics, Cen said Saltian Port is accelerating the construction of a smart terminal. This includes using artificial intelligence to analyse simultaneous operations of multiple ships and employing 5G networks for more precise control of crane systems. Operators no longer need to work outdoors in driver cabs for long periods but can remotely control large loading and unloading equipment from a control room, greatly improving the efficiency and reliability of transport, loading, unloading and distribution.
Rail-sea intermodal transport is an indispensable element of modern logistics. Cen noted that Saltian Port is the only Shenzhen port where railway trains can enter directly. Goods transported by rail from Chongqing, Chengdu and other inland areas to Saltian Port can then be transferred by barge to Hong Kong's Kwai Tsing Container Terminals for export to international markets. This model significantly shortens transport times and boosts the efficiency of exports from China's western regions.
Saltian International is a member of the Hutchison Ports network under the CK Hutchison group. Shenzhen's 15th Five-Year Plan outline emphasises strengthening cooperation between Saltian Port and Hong Kong's Kwai Tsing Port. Currently, six barges operate daily between Saltian and Hong Kong, completing two-way cargo transport in about six to eight hours. Cen said the two ports are highly complementary and can further develop inland cargo sources, jointly realising the 'Saltian-Kwai Tsing' hub function to support high-quality development of the country's foreign trade.

summary: 幻彩咏香江即将结束，香港计划举办最大规模的冬季节中国劳工布告栏 星期二, 10 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工英文新闻 香港计划在幻彩咏香江接近尾声时举办最大规模的冬季节 香港将举办最大规模的冬季旅游活动，在三个地区扩大节日设施，并升级除夕夜烟花表演。历时22年的《幻彩咏香江》将于11月18日完结。香港旅游发展局宣布，香港正准备举办迄今为止最大规模的冬季旅游活动
content:
幻彩咏香江即将结束，香港计划举办最大规模的冬季节中国劳工公告栏
2026 年 11 月 10 日，星期二 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻（英文）
幻彩咏香江即将结束 香港计划举办最大规模的冬季节
香港将举办最大规模的冬季旅游活动，在三个地区扩大节日设施，并升级除夕夜烟花表演。历时22年的《幻彩咏香江》将于11月18日完结。
香港旅游发展局11月10日宣布，香港正准备举办迄今为止最广泛的冬季旅游活动。 2026年香港冬日节将以多区节庆装置、全城零售促销，以及以香港特别行政区成立30周年为主题的升级版除夕烟花汇演。
旅游发展局主席林建岳在发布会上表示，该计划将巩固香港作为亚洲首选冬季度假胜地的地位。该倡议代表了旅游主管部门、主要商业地产开发商、金融赞助商和零售协会之间的联合努力，旨在推动当地消费并推广深度文化体验。
其中一个核心特色是去年在中环首次亮相的香港冬季仙境景点的扩建。旅游发展局再次与置地公司合作，推出中环展示中心，另外两个节庆中心也将在其他地区开业。尖沙咀将在保诚集团冠名下举办一场装置展，而铜锣湾则将设有与希慎兴业共同开发的主题中心。每一个都将展示独特的视觉概念和协调的照明性能。
冬季庆祝活动定于 11 月 18 日晚开始，届时将提供超过 100 项季节性折扣、香港独家餐饮优惠以及精选的当地纪念品。当晚还将举行《幻彩咏香江》的告别演出，这是一个在维多利亚港上演了 22 年的多媒体灯光和音响作品。最终的表演将采用特殊的烟火组件，为明年首次亮相的一系列新的海滨灯光项目铺平道路。
一年一度的跨年倒计时烟花汇演，围绕即将到来的香港特别行政区成立30周年，规模将大幅提升。旅游发展局向香港置地、保诚集团、希慎兴业、优质旅游服务协会和支付宝等主要商业伙伴表示感谢，并指出企业的协作支持对于举办香港历史上规模最大的季节性展示会至关重要。

Hong Kong plans largest WinterFest as Symphony of Lights nears end
Hong Kong will stage its biggest winter tourism campaign, with expanded festive installations in three districts and an upgraded New Year's Eve fireworks show. The long-running A Symphony of Lights will end on 18 November after 22 years.
Hong Kong is preparing to stage its most extensive winter tourism campaign to date, the Hong Kong Tourism Board announced on 10 November. The 2026 edition of the Hong Kong WinterFest will feature multi-district festive installations, citywide retail promotions, and an upgraded New Year's Eve fireworks display themed around the 30th anniversary of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
Speaking at the launch event, Tourism Board Chairman Peter Lam Kin-ngok said the programme would consolidate Hong Kong's standing as the premier winter holiday destination in Asia. The initiative represents a unified effort between tourism authorities, major commercial property developers, financial sponsors, and retail associations to drive local spending and promote in-depth cultural experiences.
A central feature is the expansion of the Hong Kong Winter Wonderlands attraction, which debuted in Central last year. The Tourism Board has partnered again with Hongkong Land to present the Central showcase, while two additional festive hubs will open in other districts. Tsim Sha Tsui will host an installation under the title sponsorship of Prudential, while Causeway Bay will feature a themed hub developed with Hysan. Each will showcase distinct visual concepts and coordinated illumination performances.
The winter festivities are scheduled to commence on the evening of 18 November, accompanied by more than one hundred seasonal discounts, Hong Kong-exclusive dining specials, and curated local souvenirs. That evening will also mark the farewell performance of A Symphony of Lights, the multimedia light and sound production that has run for 22 years across Victoria Harbour. The final show will incorporate special pyrotechnic components, paving the way for a new series of harbourfront light projects set to debut next year.
The annual New Year's Eve countdown fireworks display will undergo a major scale enhancement, centring on the upcoming 30th anniversary of the establishment of the Hong Kong SAR. The Tourism Board expressed gratitude toward key commercial partners, including Hongkong Land, Prudential, Hysan, the Quality Tourism Services Association, and Alipay, noting that collaborative corporate support has been vital in staging the largest seasonal showcase in the city's history.

title: Neros to expand domestic drone production with $450M Pentagon loan

content:
总部位于加利福尼亚州的无人机制造商 Neros Technologies 是国防部小型无人机作战竞赛的领跑者，该公司从国防部获得了 4.5 亿美元的有条件贷款，用于扩大小型无人机零部件的国内制造。 Neros 增长主管 Ross Pederson 在接受《军事时报》采访时称，美国小型无人机行业的扩张“为美国纳税人带来了巨大利益”。他说：“我认为你不必太努力地让自己相信小型无人机在未来的战争中将非常非常重要。” “如果你看看以前的现状，那就是 99% 的产品都是中国制造的，这对美国来说是站不住脚的。”国防部战略资本办公室（OSC）提供了这笔贷款。 Neros 表示将额外投入 1.65 亿美元用于扩建，使总投资达到 6.15 亿美元。佩德森认为，OSC 向 Neros 和无人机制造商 PDW 提供的贷款（7 月份获得了 8.2 亿美元的贷款）将增强美国工业。他表示，中国“完全主导”了该行业，中国公司提供了绝大多数用于组装无人机的零部件。
OSC 主任兼国防部副部长高级顾问 David Lorch 在解释向 Neros 提供贷款的原因时表示，该公司“已经展示了设计、制造和提供卓越小型无人机系统的能力”。该公司是五角大楼无人机优势计划的领导者之一，该计划旨在寻找最优质、最实惠的小型作战无人机。“OSC 的投资将增强 Neros 制造无人机和对无人机系统至关重要的组件的能力，”洛尔奇在一份声明中补充道。过去一年，联邦政府还采取了其他措施来扩大国内小型无人机产业，从发起高调的竞赛到对进口无人机零部件征收关税。尽管特朗普政府对消费品广泛征收关税引起了批评，但无人机行业专家表示，进口关税有助于鼓励企业寻求国内替代品。 10 月，《无人机战士》一书的作者、无人机公司 POWERUS 的负责人布雷特·维利科维奇 (Brett Velicovich) 告诉《军事时报》，对无人机零部件征收关税是“白宫几十年来所做的最明智的事情之一”，该书记录了他在战斗中使用小型无人机的军事经验。他认为，美国通过出口限制给国内产业戴上了“手铐”，而中国面临的限制较少。
他说，这种不平衡帮助中国占领了小型无人机及其零部件全球绝大多数市场。维利科维奇表示，关税造成了零部件的瓶颈，“对每个人来说都很难”。但他认为，他们还推动国内企业“现在专注于符合（国防授权法）的零部件”，并“迫使我们所有人寻找新的供应链”。 “最终，这对美国有利，因为我们不能继续依赖中国。我们不能继续依赖这些系统，”他说。 2025 年 6 月 26 日，在阿拉斯加州费尔班克斯举行的国防创新单元测试活动中，Neros Technologies 首席执行官 Soren Monroe-Anderson（中）驾驶该公司的一架 Archer 无人机。 （考特尼·阿尔本）但据报道，关税不一定是军事客户国内采购的主要驱动力

【原文 English Original】
California-based drone maker Neros Technologies , a frontrunner in a Defense Department competition for small drones for combat, received a $450 million conditional loan from the DoD to expand domestic manufacturing of small drone components. In an interview with Military Times, Ross Pederson, Neros’ head of growth, called the expansion of the U.S. small drone industry “a huge benefit to the American taxpayer.” “I don’t think you have to squint too hard to convince yourself that small drones are going to be very, very important in the future of warfare,” he said. “And if you look at the status quo ante, which is that 99% of them are made in China, that’s not a tenable place for the U.S. to be.” The Defense Department’s Office of Strategic Capital, or OSC, provided the loan. Neros said it will commit an additional $165 million to the expansion, which brings the total investment to $615 million. Pederson argued that OSC loans to Neros and drone maker PDW, which received an $820 million loan in July, will strengthen the U.S. industry. China has “completely dominated” the sector, he said, with Chinese companies supplying the vast majority of components used to assemble drones. Explaining its reasoning for giving Neros the loan, David Lorch, director of the OSC and senior advisor to the deputy secretary of defense, said the company “has already demonstrated an ability to design, manufacture and deliver exceptional small unmanned aircraft systems.” The company is one of the leaders in the Pentagon’s Drone Dominance Program , a competition that seeks to find the best quality, most affordable small drone for combat. “OSC’s investment will turbocharge Neros’ ability to manufacture drones and components critical for the production of drone systems,” Lorch added in a statement . The federal government has taken other steps over the past year to expand the domestic small-drone industry, ranging from launching high-profile competitions to imposing tariffs on imported drone components . Although the Trump administration’s broad use of tariffs on consumer goods has drawn criticism , drone industry experts say the import duties have helped encourage companies to seek domestic alternatives. In October, Brett Velicovich — author of Drone Warrior, which documents his military experience using small drones in combat, and head of drone company POWERUS — told Military Times that tariffs on drone components were “one of the smartest things the White House has done in decades.” He argued that the U.S. had put “handcuffs” on its domestic industry through export restrictions, while China faced fewer constraints. That imbalance, he said, helped China capture the overwhelming majority of the global market for small drones and their components. The tariffs have created a bottleneck for components that has “been hard on everyone,” Velicovich said. But he argued that they have also pushed domestic companies to “now focus on ( National Defense Authorization Act )-compliant parts” and “forces all of us to find new supply chains.” “In the end, it’s what’s good for America because we can’t continue to be reliant on China. We can’t continue to be reliant on those systems,” he said. Neros Technologies CEO Soren Monroe-Anderson, center, flies one of the company’s Archer drones on June 26, 2025, during a Defense Innovation Unit test event in Fairbanks, Alaska. (Courtney Albon) But tariffs aren’t necessarily the main driver of domestic sourcing for military customers, according to Pederson. The Defense Department has long been prohibited from purchasing drones containing electronic components from certain foreign countries, including China, he said. “When it comes to that specific customer set, the tariffs aren’t necessarily the driving factor. It’s really the prohibition that the Department of War has on purchasing Chinese electronics,” he said. Before receiving the loan, Pederson explained, Neros didn’t manufacture its own components. Instead, it contracted other companies to manufacture parts that it then used to assemble drones. That is expected to change as the company expands its domestic production capabilities. Neros has already expanded its in-house motor production and will soon begin manufacturing surface-mount technology components, which are used to populate circuit boards, Pederson said. “By late next year, somewhere in the like 80% by dollar value of the drone should be made in-house, like in the same physical space where the drones are being assembled,” he said. Pederson declined to provide specifics about the loan’s terms, including its interest rate and repayment timeline, but he said it is not subject to loan forgiveness and that the Defense Department has manufacturing goals for the company. “They’re all centered on making these components in the United States and making them available broadly to the market, not just to ourselves,” he said.

Kenya: TikTok Removes 750,000 Videos in Kenya Over Content Violations
Nairobi — TikTok removed more than 750,000 videos in Kenya for violating its community guidelines in the second quarter of 2026, highlighting the growing operational and regulatory demands facing digital platforms as online content consumption expands.
The short-video platform said it took down 750,185 videos between April and June, with 99.8 percent removed before users reported them, while 93.8 percent were taken down within 24 hours of publication.
The removals point to the increasing reliance on artificial intelligence and automated moderation systems to manage content at scale, as technology companies face mounting pressure to address misinformation, harmful material and online safety concerns.
TikTok also interrupted 80,640 LIVE sessions in Kenya during the period for violations of its community guidelines, while removing more than 46,000 accounts suspected to belong to children below the age of 13.
Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn
"About 99.8 percent of the videos removed in Kenya were taken down proactively before anyone reported them, and 93.8 percent were removed within 24 hours of being posted," the company said in its Q2 Community Guidelines Enforcement Report.
Globally, TikTok removed approximately 188.3 million videos out of more than 42.2 billion videos published during the quarter, representing about 0.4 percent of total uploads.
Automated systems accounted for 97.4 percent of global video removals, underscoring the platform's growing dependence on artificial intelligence to identify and enforce content violations.
However, the company reinstated approximately 6.3 million videos globally following successful appeals, raising questions about the accuracy of automated moderation and the balance between content safety and users' freedom of expression.
In Kenya, nearly 11,000 videos were removed under TikTok's policies on edited media and artificial intelligence-generated content as the platform stepped up efforts to address the risks associated with synthetic media.
The company has also introduced an in-app AI Literacy Hub in Kenya to educate users on identifying AI-generated content and using the technology responsibly.
The developments come as digital platforms face increasing scrutiny over child protection, misinformation and the economic and social consequences of harmful online content.
TikTok said it requires creators to label realistic AI-generated material and uses Content Credentials technology to help identify content created or significantly altered using artificial intelligence.

title: At COP31, World Food Programme Urges Use of Innovative Finance to Prevent Climate Shocks From Becoming Hunger Emergencies
summary: Africa: At COP31, World Food Programme Urges Use of Innovative Finance to Prevent Climate Shocks From Becoming Hunger Emergencies - allAfrica.com Africa: At COP31, World Food Programme Urges Use of Innovative Finance to Prevent Climate Shoc
content:
Africa: At COP31, World Food Programme Urges Use of Innovative Finance to Prevent Climate Shocks From Becoming Hunger Emergencies - allAfrica.com
Africa: At COP31, World Food Programme Urges Use of Innovative Finance to Prevent Climate Shocks From Becoming Hunger Emergencies
Around the venue at COP31.
United Nations World Food Programme (Rome)
Areas already affected by conflict and economic instability face climate shocks that risk pushing millions more people into acute food insecurity. WFP analysis projects that the current El Niño could push at least 49 million more people into acute food insecurity by the end of 2027. The phenomenon is expected to reach peak intensity between October and December 2026, while its impact on planting seasons, harvests and food prices could continue into early 2028.
These risks are already visible across regions. Drought is affecting growing seasons in Central America's Dry Corridor, while parts of the Sahel and East Africa are also experiencing severe dryness. Southern Africa faces the threat of drought during a crucial growing season, while heavy rain and flooding could affect the Horn of Africa and parts of South America.
"With floods, droughts and storms striking so often, vulnerable families have little time to recover," said Carl Skau, WFP's Deputy Executive Director and Chief Operating Officer. "El Niño will intensify that pressure, but because it can be predicted, we have a chance to act before crops fail, livelihoods are lost, and hunger sets in. COP31 must seize this window and turn it into faster, more accessible financing for the countries and communities on the front lines of disasters."
WFP is the UN's largest user of pre-arranged financing, drawing on anticipatory action, insurance, and contingency funding to deliver support before or immediately after an emergency. At COP31, WFP is working closely with other UN agencies to scale-up pre-arranged financing and strengthen collaboration, with the aim of lowering costs and making scarce resources go further.
Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines
WFP is acting before shocks hit. Between January and September, WFP reached 4.9 million people with early warnings and provided more than 1.5 million with assistance ahead of forecast floods, storms, and droughts, backed by US$46.2 million in pre-arranged funds.
However, these approaches remain far below the scale required. Pre-arranged mechanisms account for less than two percent of global humanitarian financing.
Scale up predictable, pre-arranged financing that can be released before forecasted hazards escalate into disasters.
Make finance more accessible to fragile, conflict-affected and highly food-insecure countries.
Invest in nationally led early warning, anticipatory action, disaster risk management, and shock-responsive social protection systems.

content:
困扰英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋的丑闻不再仅仅是硅谷最有权势的人之一是否与涉嫌中国间谍有染的问题。这也是一个关于白宫知道什么以及它可能选择忽视什么的问题。在《纽约时报》的爆炸性报道之后，黄仁勋和英伟达于周日证实了这一关系。 Alice Huang（与 Jensen 无关系）是此次爆料的核心女性，她是新加坡数据中心公司 Megaspeed 的一名高管，该公司是 Nvidia 芯片的主要客户。据报道，美国情报监视显示，她一直在直接向中国政府提供信息。目前尚不清楚的是，有多少敏感信息可能被泄露，黄对他所见的那个女人了解多少，以及为什么美国情报官员显然没有警告他她涉嫌与北京的关系。这些答案可能会对黄和白宫造成严重损害。乔治城大学安全与新兴技术中心研究员萨姆·布雷斯尼克表示，“很多人都非常清楚，[黄仁勋]将成为中国情报收集的目标”，因为他与唐纳德·特朗普总统关系密切，而且他领导的公司是“美中人工智能竞争的核心”。英伟达不断变化的故事 承认这件事也与英伟达和黄本人之前描述他与爱丽丝黄的关系的方式相矛盾。
就在 10 月 29 日，公司发言人约翰·里佐 (John Rizzo) 将他们的互动描述为例行业务往来，而黄坚称这些互动“完全正常，并不罕见”。黄现在面临英伟达董事会的调查，尽管董事们在周日的一份声明中表示，他们“没有理由相信国家安全或英伟达的机密受到损害”，并表示“对詹森和他的领导团队充满信心”。董事会的调查可能是黄仁勋最不担心的事情。这位有权势的首席执行官面临着国会两党审查的前景，同时人们对他在华盛顿的影响力以及他在英伟达的未来也提出了越来越多的质疑。国会希望得到解答的问题 上周晚些时候，三名众议院议员——共和党人布莱恩·马斯特 (Brian Mast)、约翰·穆勒纳尔 (John Moolenaar) 和埃里克·克劳福德 (Eric Crawford)——给黄致了一封信，要求他参加在华盛顿特区举行的有关此事的闭门听证会。周一，当 Fast Company 询问黄是否打算参加时，英伟达拒绝公开回应。明年，民主党控制的新国会可能会传唤包括黄仁勋在内的一些科技领袖就他们与特朗普的往来作证。周一，特拉华州参议员克里斯·库恩斯呼吁对黄仁勋和英伟达进行调查，以确定国家安全是否受到损害。 “我们需要关于人工智能亿万富翁和特朗普政府之间关系的答案，”他在 X 上写道。
当民主党一月份控制国会时，库恩斯将担任参议院外交关系委员会主席，这赋予他相当大的权力来寻求这些答案。当然还有很多事情需要调查。其一，我们不知道 Alice Huang 是否从黄仁勋那里获取了敏感信息并将其传输给中国政府。布雷斯尼克表示，黄仁勋和他的设备可能掌握了多种有价值的信息，包括即将推出的英伟达芯片的商业秘密、该公司的研究策略或美国政府限制中国的计划

【原文 English Original】
The scandal engulfing Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is no longer simply a question of whether one of Silicon Valley’s most powerful men had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. It’s also a question of what the White House knew—and what it might have chosen to overlook. Huang and Nvidia confirmed the relationship Sunday, following a bombshell New York Times report . Alice Huang (no relation to Jensen)—the woman at the center of the revelations—is an executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed, a major customer of Nvidia chips. U.S. intelligence surveillance reportedly showed that she had been funneling information directly to the Chinese government. What remains unclear is how much sensitive information may have been compromised, what Huang knew about the woman he was seeing, and why U.S. intelligence officials apparently failed to warn him about her suspected ties to Beijing. The answers could prove deeply damaging to both Huang and the White House. “It was pretty clear to a lot of people that [Jensen Huang] would be a target of Chinese intelligence collection,” given his proximity to President Donald Trump and his leadership of a company that is “central to the U.S.-China AI competition,” says Sam Bresnick, a research fellow at Georgetown University’s Center for Security and Emerging Technology. Nvidia’s changing story The admission of the affair also contradicts how Nvidia and Huang himself had previously characterized his ties to Alice Huang. As recently as October 29, company spokesperson John Rizzo described their interactions as routine business dealings, while Huang insisted they were “completely normal and not unusual.” Huang now faces an investigation by Nvidia’s board, although directors said in a statement Sunday that they had “no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised” and expressed “confidence in Jensen and his leadership team.” The board’s investigation may be the least of Huang’s worries. The powerful CEO faces the prospect of bipartisan congressional scrutiny, along with mounting questions about his influence in Washington and his future at Nvidia. The questions Congress wants answered Late last week, three House members—Republicans Brian Mast, John Moolenaar, and Eric Crawford—sent Huang a letter requesting that he attend a closed-door hearing on the matter in Washington, D.C. Asked by Fast Company on Monday whether Huang intends to attend, Nvidia declined to answer on the record. Next year, the new Democrat-controlled Congress will likely call a number of tech leaders, including Huang, to testify about their dealings with Trump. On Monday, Senator Chris Coons of Delaware called for an investigation into Huang and Nvidia to determine whether national security had been compromised. “We need answers about the relationship between AI billionaires and the Trump administration,” he wrote on X. Coons is poised to chair the Senate Foreign Relations Committee when Democrats take control of Congress in January, giving him considerable power to pursue those answers. There is certainly plenty to investigate. For one, we don’t know whether Alice Huang obtained sensitive information from Jensen Huang and transmitted it to the Chinese government. Bresnick says Huang and his devices may have been in possession of several types of valuable information, including trade secrets about upcoming Nvidia chips, the company’s research strategies, or U.S. government plans to restrict China’s access to advanced AI technology. “Did he provide information to her about the Trump administration’s thinking on AI—U.S.-China competition, export controls, and trade policy more broadly?” Bresnick asks. “Because if [the Chinese] have greater texture on what the administration’s thinking, it’s easier for them to position themselves.” (The White House did not respond to Fast Company ’s request for comment.) It’s also unclear what Huang knew about the woman, and when. He certainly knew he was having an extramarital affair with an executive at a customer company, which violates Nvidia’s code of conduct. But we don’t know when he learned that she was a suspected spy. What did the White House know? Then there’s the question of when U.S. intelligence learned about Alice Huang’s activities. According to the reporting, the U.S. government had known about her ties to Beijing for months. Bresnick finds it strange that intelligence officials apparently failed to warn the Nvidia CEO, given his close relationship with the president and his position atop a company developing some of the world’s most advanced AI technology. “The fact that this potentially could have been at risk” makes the apparent lack of intervention all the more puzzling, he says. One possibility is that the White House prevented intelligence agencies from warning Huang about the suspected spy. After all, the Trump administration has compelling reasons to keep Huang and Nvidia out of the headlines. The stock market’s strong performance has been a central selling point for the administration, and Nvidia is the crown jewel of the AI-related stocks that have driven much of its growth. AI and AI-related companies accounted for as much as half of the market’s gains this year, according to a new J.P. Morgan report . The White House may have had an even more direct financial incentive. The federal government stands to collect revenue from Nvidia’s AI chip sales to China. Last year, Huang persuaded Trump to allow Nvidia to sell its H200 chips in China, provided the U.S. government received a 25% cut of the sales. Huang also reportedly discussed selling Nvidia’s top-of-the-line Blackwell graphics processing units in China, but that proposal was ultimately shut down over national security concerns. In August 2025, Huang agreed to give the U.S. government a 15% cut in exchange for permission to sell the lower-performing H20 chip to China. “Was the government hoping to get a bunch of money from these deals, from Chinese buyers getting access to these things?” Bresnick asks. Nvidia’s influence comes under scrutiny Alice Huang’s employer, Megaspeed, became an official Nvidia Cloud Partner in November 2023 and purchased more than $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over roughly two years, according to the Associated Press . But the company was also under investigation by the U.S. Commerce Department over suspicions that it was funneling restricted AI chips to China. A New York Times investigation last year found that Megaspeed’s offices in Singapore and Malaysia were largely empty, while many of its executives are based in China. Commerce Department officials who spoke to The Times even described finding boxes of restricted Nvidia chips in a Megaspeed facility in Malaysia. On Monday, The Times reported that the Commerce Department’s investigation came to an abrupt halt last year after Nvidia’s general counsel, Tim Teter, contacted investigators seeking information about the case. Teter reportedly told them that Jeff Kessler, a senior Commerce official appointed by Trump, had given Nvidia permission to reach out. The communication alarmed investigators, some of whom worried that Kessler’s involvement had potentially compromised their work. The case was subsequently transferred to the Justice Department, which is now conducting a criminal investigation into Megaspeed. Officials familiar with the matter told The Times the transfer was intended to prevent the investigation from being compromised. There is no evidence that Kessler instructed investigators to share information with Nvidia, but the unusual circumstances of the transfer have raised questions about the company’s influence over the very officials responsible for policing its chip sales. For Bresnick, the investigation also raises questions about how Megaspeed was able to acquire billions of dollars’ worth of advanced Nvidia chips despite suspicions about its operations. “We had no idea where those chips went,” he says. Together, the revelations raise questions about whether Nvidia’s political influence complicated the government’s response to potential national security threats. This all comes at a politically sensitive moment: Corruption was a major factor in voters’ decisions in the midterms, and Nvidia now risks becoming entangled in a controversy that could damage its standing in Washington. Despite Huang’s scandal, Creative Strategies chairman and longtime analyst Tim Bajarin suggests those calling for his ouster could meet serious opposition.  “Removal of Jensen would be a very difficult decision because he is the heart and soul of Nvidia,” Bajarin says. “I have met with Jensen many times over the years, and he was always the smartest guy in the room. More importantly, he has the global vision for Nvidia’s future and needs to be the one driving their future.”

title: Neros to expand domestic drone production with $450M Pentagon loan

content:
总部位于加利福尼亚州的无人机制造商 Neros Technologies 是国防部小型无人机作战竞赛的领跑者，该公司从国防部获得了 4.5 亿美元的有条件贷款，用于扩大小型无人机零部件的国内制造。 Neros 增长主管 Ross Pederson 在接受《军事时报》采访时称，美国小型无人机行业的扩张“为美国纳税人带来了巨大利益”。他说：“我认为你不必太努力地让自己相信小型无人机在未来的战争中将非常非常重要。” “如果你看看以前的现状，那就是 99% 的产品都是中国制造的，这对美国来说是站不住脚的。”国防部战略资本办公室（OSC）提供了这笔贷款。 Neros 表示将额外投入 1.65 亿美元用于扩建，使总投资达到 6.15 亿美元。佩德森认为，OSC 向 Neros 和无人机制造商 PDW 提供的贷款（7 月份获得了 8.2 亿美元的贷款）将增强美国工业。他表示，中国“完全主导”了该行业，中国公司提供了绝大多数用于组装无人机的零部件。
OSC 主任兼国防部副部长高级顾问 David Lorch 在解释向 Neros 提供贷款的原因时表示，该公司“已经展示了设计、制造和提供卓越小型无人机系统的能力”。该公司是五角大楼无人机优势计划的领导者之一，该计划旨在寻找最优质、最实惠的小型作战无人机。“OSC 的投资将增强 Neros 制造无人机和对无人机系统至关重要的组件的能力，”洛尔奇在一份声明中补充道。过去一年，联邦政府还采取了其他措施来扩大国内小型无人机产业，从发起高调的竞赛到对进口无人机零部件征收关税。尽管特朗普政府对消费品广泛征收关税引起了批评，但无人机行业专家表示，进口关税有助于鼓励企业寻求国内替代品。 10 月，《无人机战士》一书的作者、无人机公司 POWERUS 的负责人布雷特·维利科维奇 (Brett Velicovich) 告诉《军事时报》，对无人机零部件征收关税是“白宫几十年来所做的最明智的事情之一”，该书记录了他在战斗中使用小型无人机的军事经验。他认为，美国通过出口限制给国内产业戴上了“手铐”，而中国面临的限制较少。
他说，这种不平衡帮助中国占领了小型无人机及其零部件全球绝大多数市场。维利科维奇表示，关税造成了零部件的瓶颈，“对每个人来说都很难”。但他认为，他们还推动国内企业“现在专注于符合（国防授权法）的零部件”，并“迫使我们所有人寻找新的供应链”。 “最终，这对美国有利，因为我们不能继续依赖中国。我们不能继续依赖这些系统，”他说。 2025 年 6 月 26 日，在阿拉斯加州费尔班克斯举行的国防创新单元测试活动中，Neros Technologies 首席执行官 Soren Monroe-Anderson（中）驾驶该公司的一架 Archer 无人机。 （考特尼·阿尔本）但据报道，关税不一定是军事客户国内采购的主要驱动力

【原文 English Original】
California-based drone maker Neros Technologies , a frontrunner in a Defense Department competition for small drones for combat, received a $450 million conditional loan from the DoD to expand domestic manufacturing of small drone components. In an interview with Military Times, Ross Pederson, Neros’ head of growth, called the expansion of the U.S. small drone industry “a huge benefit to the American taxpayer.” “I don’t think you have to squint too hard to convince yourself that small drones are going to be very, very important in the future of warfare,” he said. “And if you look at the status quo ante, which is that 99% of them are made in China, that’s not a tenable place for the U.S. to be.” The Defense Department’s Office of Strategic Capital, or OSC, provided the loan. Neros said it will commit an additional $165 million to the expansion, which brings the total investment to $615 million. Pederson argued that OSC loans to Neros and drone maker PDW, which received an $820 million loan in July, will strengthen the U.S. industry. China has “completely dominated” the sector, he said, with Chinese companies supplying the vast majority of components used to assemble drones. Explaining its reasoning for giving Neros the loan, David Lorch, director of the OSC and senior advisor to the deputy secretary of defense, said the company “has already demonstrated an ability to design, manufacture and deliver exceptional small unmanned aircraft systems.” The company is one of the leaders in the Pentagon’s Drone Dominance Program , a competition that seeks to find the best quality, most affordable small drone for combat. “OSC’s investment will turbocharge Neros’ ability to manufacture drones and components critical for the production of drone systems,” Lorch added in a statement . The federal government has taken other steps over the past year to expand the domestic small-drone industry, ranging from launching high-profile competitions to imposing tariffs on imported drone components . Although the Trump administration’s broad use of tariffs on consumer goods has drawn criticism , drone industry experts say the import duties have helped encourage companies to seek domestic alternatives. In October, Brett Velicovich — author of Drone Warrior, which documents his military experience using small drones in combat, and head of drone company POWERUS — told Military Times that tariffs on drone components were “one of the smartest things the White House has done in decades.” He argued that the U.S. had put “handcuffs” on its domestic industry through export restrictions, while China faced fewer constraints. That imbalance, he said, helped China capture the overwhelming majority of the global market for small drones and their components. The tariffs have created a bottleneck for components that has “been hard on everyone,” Velicovich said. But he argued that they have also pushed domestic companies to “now focus on ( National Defense Authorization Act )-compliant parts” and “forces all of us to find new supply chains.” “In the end, it’s what’s good for America because we can’t continue to be reliant on China. We can’t continue to be reliant on those systems,” he said. Neros Technologies CEO Soren Monroe-Anderson, center, flies one of the company’s Archer drones on June 26, 2025, during a Defense Innovation Unit test event in Fairbanks, Alaska. (Courtney Albon) But tariffs aren’t necessarily the main driver of domestic sourcing for military customers, according to Pederson. The Defense Department has long been prohibited from purchasing drones containing electronic components from certain foreign countries, including China, he said. “When it comes to that specific customer set, the tariffs aren’t necessarily the driving factor. It’s really the prohibition that the Department of War has on purchasing Chinese electronics,” he said. Before receiving the loan, Pederson explained, Neros didn’t manufacture its own components. Instead, it contracted other companies to manufacture parts that it then used to assemble drones. That is expected to change as the company expands its domestic production capabilities. Neros has already expanded its in-house motor production and will soon begin manufacturing surface-mount technology components, which are used to populate circuit boards, Pederson said. “By late next year, somewhere in the like 80% by dollar value of the drone should be made in-house, like in the same physical space where the drones are being assembled,” he said. Pederson declined to provide specifics about the loan’s terms, including its interest rate and repayment timeline, but he said it is not subject to loan forgiveness and that the Defense Department has manufacturing goals for the company. “They’re all centered on making these components in the United States and making them available broadly to the market, not just to ourselves,” he said.

title: A Scandal at the Center of the Economy

content:
考虑到美国和中国之间对人工智能竞赛的痴迷，你可能会想象，领导人工智能领域最重要公司的男性被发现与一名据信是中国间谍的女性发生婚外情的消息会引发前所未有的愤怒和谴责。你可以想象，这种鲁莽的行为一旦被发现，可能会导致人们广泛呼吁立即辞职并进行深入调查——不仅是高管，而是整个公司。干草叉等等。那么，奇怪的是，当英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋与一名同时也是北京国家安全部资产的中国女商人发生恋情的消息传出时，硅谷和华盛顿特区的知名派系似乎感到困惑。 “即使是不可思议的人也会犯错误，”亿万富翁对冲基金经理比尔·阿克曼昨天在 X 上发帖说。 “我们都应该支持他和他的家人。继续前进。”风险投资家肖恩·马奎尔对黄的处境进行了五点分析，指出这位首席执行官做了一些“极其愚蠢”且“对美国不利”的事情，但“我的猜测是他没有恶意”。然后他辩称，“我相信詹森对于美国人工智能的领导地位是不可替代的。”埃隆·马斯克同意了。从那时起，在我们了解丑闻的所有事实之前写的帖子变得更加荒谬，包括以黄的孩子现在已经成年为由为黄的外遇辩护。
[阅读：美国无法承受人工智能衰退]当天晚些时候，唐纳德·特朗普回应了黄仁勋继续担任首席执行官的呼吁。他称黄仁勋是“一个值得尊敬的人”。这位总统自己也有过婚外情，并被众多女性可信地指控犯有性犯罪，但他听起来并不在意。 “我认为他可能有一个借口，”特朗普补充道。英伟达的董事会似乎也同样恭敬。它宣布对这一事件进行独立调查，但也强调“没有理由相信国家安全或 NVIDIA 机密受到损害”，并且“对 Jensen 及其领导团队充满信心”。黄则昨天发表声明承认此事，并表示将配合调查。人们很容易认为这只不过是有权势的人在捍卫自己的同类——这是在紧迫的技术地缘政治安全要求之前兄弟的典型例子。但这种解释忽略了黄仁勋和英伟达在美国政治和全球金融体系中的中心地位。英伟达的芯片可以说是人工智能热潮中最重要的基础设施组成部分；如果没有这项技术，世界各地的 OpenAI 和 Anthropics 将无法训练或驱动他们的模型——有报道称，亿万富翁们已恳求黄仁勋给予更多 Nvidia 芯片的分配。
这种强烈的需求使英伟达成为金融巨头。 5月份，其市值为5.7万亿美元，超过除美国和中国以外的所有经济体。去年，我和我的同事 Matteo Wong 将美国描述为英伟达国家，就像沙特阿拉伯是石油国家一样。这是因为，近年来，该公司已成为其他人工智能公司的最大投资者之一；截至 7 月，Nvidia 宣布其股权投资价值约 990 亿美元，投资对象包括 OpenAI、Anthropic、SpaceX 等公司以及 CoreWeave 等数据中心提供商。这是一种循环投资方式，公司向 Nvidia 支付巨额资金

【原文 English Original】
Given the obsession over the AI race between the United States and China, you might imagine that news of the man leading the most important company in AI being caught in an extramarital relationship with a woman believed to be a Chinese spy would spark outrage and excoriation without parallel. You could suppose that such reckless behavior, upon discovery, might lead to widespread calls for immediate resignation and for deep investigation—not just of the executive, but the entire company. Pitchforks, et cetera. It is curious, then, that, as news came out that the Nvidia CEO, Jensen Huang, had had a romantic relationship with a Chinese businesswoman who was also an asset of Beijing’s Ministry of State Security, notable factions of Silicon Valley and Washington, D.C., seemed nonplussed. “Even incredible humans make mistakes,” Bill Ackman, the billionaire hedge-fund manager, posted on X yesterday. “We should all support him and his family. Onward.” The venture capitalist Shaun Maguire offered a five-point analysis of Huang’s situation, noting that the CEO did something “incredibly dumb” and “bad for America,” but that “my guess is there was no bad intention.” He then argued, “I believe Jensen is irreplaceable for America’s AI leadership.” Elon Musk agreed. From there, the posts, written before we know all the facts of the scandal, got only more absurd , including defending Huang’s affair on the grounds that his kids are adults now. [ Read: America can’t afford an AI recession ] Later in the day, Donald Trump echoed calls for Huang to stay on as CEO. He called Huang “an honorable guy.” The president, who has had extramarital affairs of his own and is credibly accused of sexual crimes by numerous women, sounded unbothered. “I think he probably has an excuse for it,” Trump added. Nvidia’s board of directors seemed equally deferential. It announced an independent investigation into the incident but also stressed that it has “no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised” and that it “has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team.” Huang, for his part, issued a statement yesterday acknowledging the affair and noting that he would cooperate with the investigation. It’s tempting to see this as little more than powerful men defending their kind—a classic example of bros before pressing technological-geopolitical security imperatives. But that explanation misses both Huang’s and Nvidia’s centrality in American politics and the global financial system. Nvidia’s chips are arguably the most important infrastructure component of the AI boom; without the tech, the OpenAIs and Anthropics of the world would be unable to train or power their models—reporting suggests that billionaires have begged Huang for greater allocations of Nvidia chips. This intense demand has made Nvidia a financial juggernaut; in May, its market capitalization was $5.7 trillion, which made it larger than every economy except that of the U.S. and China. Last year, my colleague Matteo Wong and I described the U.S. as an Nvidia-state, much like Saudi Arabia is a petrostate. That’s because, in recent years, the company has become one of the biggest investors of other AI companies; As of July, Nvidia announced that its equity investments valued roughly $99 billion, including in companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic, SpaceX, and data-center providers like CoreWeave. It’s a circular style of investment where companies pay Nvidia enormous sums of money for its chips and then Nvidia reinvests some of that money back into those companies and their competitors, in part so that they can continue to buy chips. You could make a strong case that Nvidia helps support big chunks of the Magnificent Seven ecosystem, the tech companies that are responsible for roughly a third of the S&P 500’s current value. According to The Economist , Nvidia stock has produced “15 cents of every dollar the American stock market has returned since 2023.” Huang, who founded Nvidia in 1993, is the company’s key figure, praised by many in the tech industry as one of the visionaries responsible for the rapid acceleration of artificial intelligence. He’s instrumental in the company’s engineering decisions, its allocation of chips, and other investments. He also has no clear successor. Outside of Silicon Valley, Huang has become a trusted adviser and ally to Trump on AI policy. Huang’s thinking on issues such as AI doomerism (he’s anti-doom) and chip allocation in China (he’s for it—a position that warrants examining, given this weekend’s revelations) influences U.S. policy. This centrality is why one tech analyst on CNBC this morning implied that replacing Huang was a comical suggestion. Huang is a singular figure: the linchpin of the company that is arguably the linchpin of the American economy. Framed another way, Nvidia has much of the financial system in a hostage situation. Huang is too big to fail. Which may be why so many people seem motivated to downplay or protect him right now. How else would one describe the prolific excuse-making for him? The information that has come out around Huang’s involvement with the alleged Chinese spy is alarming. Concerns about the relationship have been mounting for more than a year. Alice Huang (no relation to Jensen) worked for the Singaporean data-center company Megaspeed, an Nvidia client the government had been investigating regarding its potential connections to the Chinese government. As The New York Times reported today, Nvidia intervened in the U.S. Department of Commerce’s investigation of Megaspeed; the probe was subsequently halted and transferred to the Justice Department. According to the Times , Trump was briefed about Huang’s relationship roughly a year ago, including the presumption that Alice may be a spy, and “chose not to do anything with that intelligence.” In recent weeks, the Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo and Huang himself both dismissed claims that the relationship with the woman in question was unusual or romantic in any way—we now know this was untrue. It’s still unclear whether Huang disclosed any pertinent corporate or national-security secrets or whether his relationship with an alleged spy had any impact on Nvidia’s opposition to semiconductor export controls in China. But everything we know so far paints Huang, Nvidia, and government officials in a terrible light, at every turn either ignoring or obfuscating a national-security problem. As more information about the relationship comes out, lawmakers will have to choose whether to take their cues from the markets (Nvidia shares dropped 8.8 percent at one point today—a $400 billion drop in the company’s valuation) or push for more investigation. Trump, who has been reliably motivated in his presidency by the stock market, seems indebted to Nvidia’s performance in the market, as well as to AI investment in general. He’s unlikely to do anything to jeopardize that. Democrats are in a particularly interesting position, fresh off a midterm rout centered on taking a strong stance against tech oligarchs, AI, and data centers and in favor of corporate accountability. Earlier today, Senator Chris Coons said on X that he would push for an investigation into Huang and Nvidia. To press hard on Huang to resign, or to dig deeper into what he and the company knew about the relationship and when, will inevitably risk adding volatility to Nvidia’s share price and, by virtue, the larger Gordian knot of AI investment that is predicated on relentless growth and continued scale. All of this is to say that the moral case regarding Huang is much different from the one that Trump and those with a financial interest in Nvidia’s success will likely consider. This scandal holds an irony that’s especially befitting of the AI moment. Huang seemingly has cozied up to his industry’s No. 1 foe, China, the boogeyman that, by the professed logic of Silicon Valley’s AI executives, is forcing many of his peers to build a product that they fear. Instead of denouncing him, Washington and Silicon Valley are motivated to circle the wagons around Huang, in part because doing so keeps the system moving and the money flowing. The build at all costs rationale that dictates treating China’s AI prowess as an existential threat is also driving the same people to brush past an egregious dalliance with that enemy. This is the type of warped incentives that the AI race produces. Playing the game necessitates embracing preposterous risk to justify an idealized future outcome. To run this race requires its participants to withstand intense cognitive dissonance and behave in ways that make them appear ever more inscrutable and reckless to those who are not involved. If nothing else, Huang is a useful example to understand what happens when the fortunes of countries and many of its most powerful citizens are all tied up in one progressively intricate technological and financial bet. In this way, Huang is the AI boom personified, a hyperobject of a man who has wound his way into the center of the economy and whose influence, depending on how you look at it, may usher in either prosperity or untold doom.

title: Jensen Huang’s alleged honeypot scandal has inspired some top-notch memes

content:
Jensen Huang's alleged honeypot scandal has inspired some top-notch memes | TechCrunch
Jensen Huang’s alleged honeypot scandal has inspired some top-notch memes
8:34 PM PST · November 9, 2026
Jensen Huang, the CEO and co-founder of the world’s most prominent chip company, has allegedly been honey-trapped by a suspected Chinese spy, and the news has struck the internet like a match to gasoline.
Huang has long been seen as a wife guy (or so everyone assumed). He and his wife, Lori, have been together since the 1980s, and both of their children work at Nvidia. Huang has been the closest thing the tech world has to a rock star, with fans lining up for selfies and autographs. Of all the AI overlords, the leather-jacket wearing Huang has seemed like the most level-headed and least erratic, which is why this plot twist has hit so hard.
The potential fallout is mind-boggling. Nvidia looms so large over the U.S. stock market that even the company’s domestic drama is a market risk. Countless AI startups depend on Nvidia chips, so any shake-up at the top would ripple far beyond the company. And Nvidia has no publicly disclosed succession plan, so if Huang leaves, it’s unclear who’d take over.
Is this how the AI bubble bursts? It’s a question that will be answered in time, but in the meantime, a more pressing matter demands our attention: ranking the funniest memes about the scandal, with bonus points for AI images presumably generated using Nvidia chips.
There’s admittedly a lot to choose from, ranging from “500 Days of Summer” jokes to jokes about divorce lawyers to an AI-adaptation of the music video for Usher‘s song “Confessions Pt. II,” a track about cheating. Another person created a viral AI video that recreates the Coldplay concert where a startup CEO was caught on the Jumbotron hugging a colleague.
Huang publicly confessed to the affair just yesterday, so the internet has the rest of the week to get creative.

Yes, the internet is having a field day with this one.
As usual, AI-generated content is doing a lot of heavy lifting. Copyleaks, a software company that analyzes online content for signs of AI and digital manipulation, said Monday that it had seen “an explosion in AI-manipulated photos and videos of Huang and Alice Huang, ranging from memes to more subtle edits.” The tally includes at least 70 AI-related posts on X, which together drew around 8.42 million views and 64,362 engagements as of Monday morning. Those metrics have almost certainly climbed since.
